# Power Manager Fast FSM Specification

## Overview

This module is the fast-clock-domain power-management sequencing state machine. It is responsible for moving the system through power-up, normal active operation, low-power entry, and reset handling.

The module interacts with:

- A companion slow-clock power manager state machine through power-up and power-down handshakes.
- Clock and reset managers through clock-enable requests, reset requests, and reset status inputs.
- Storage and lifecycle blocks during initialization.
- The processing element through a fetch-enable output.

The module must ensure that clocks, resets, fetch enables, and initialization activities occur in the correct order, and that low-power entry is aborted or falls through when appropriate.

---

## Initial Conditions

After reset, the module shall:

- Enter a low-power resting state.
- Assert reset requests for all power domains.
- Disable all main and I/O clock requests.
- Assert the low-power indication.
- Keep the processing element fetch-enable deasserted.
- Set the reset cause to an undefined value.
- Not assert power-up acknowledge or power-down request.

The module shall remain in this state until it receives a power-up request from the companion state machine or until an internally tracked reset condition is pending.

---

## Power-Up Sequence

When a power-up request is received, or when a reset condition is already pending, the module shall perform the following sequence.

### 1. Enable Clocks

The module shall request that main and I/O clocks be enabled.

The USB clock request shall be asserted only when:

- main and I/O clock enable is requested, and
- USB clocking is enabled.

The module must wait until every clock domain reports a status consistent with its requested state:

- a domain requested to be enabled must report enabled;
- a domain requested to be disabled must report disabled.

The module shall not proceed until all clock statuses are consistent.

### 2. Release Resets

The module shall release reset requests for all power domains.

It must wait until the reset status indicates that the reset outputs have been deasserted before continuing.

### 3. Initialize OTP Storage

The module shall assert the OTP initialization request and hold it until the OTP storage reports that initialization is complete.

### 4. Initialize Life Cycle

The module shall assert the life-cycle initialization request and hold it until the life-cycle controller reports that initialization is complete.

### 5. Complete Power-Up Handshake

After life-cycle initialization completes:

- If the power-up sequence was not caused by an internally tracked reset, the module shall assert the power-up acknowledge output.
- If the power-up sequence was caused by an internally tracked reset, the module shall not assert the power-up acknowledge output.

The module shall then wait until:

- the power-up request is deasserted, or
- the power-up sequence was caused by a reset condition.

At that point, the module shall deassert the power-up acknowledge if it was asserted, and:

- assert the clear-configuration-lock output;
- assert a wakeup indication if and only if the power-up cause is a wakeup from low power and the previous reset cause was a low-power entry;
- clear the internally tracked reset-pending condition.

### 6. Strap Sampling

The module shall perform strap sampling after a cold boot or after any reset cycle that asserts all system resets.

If strap sampling has not yet been performed, the module shall assert the strap-sample output. If strap sampling has already been performed, for example after a low-power wakeup without a reset, no strap-sample output shall be generated.

### 7. ROM Integrity Check

The module shall deassert the low-power indication and clear the reset cause to none.

It shall then wait for the ROM integrity check to pass.

The ROM integrity check passes when:

- the ROM controller reports completion and reports a good result, or
- the ROM controller reports completion and the life-cycle controller indicates that both design-for-test and hardware debug enables are active.

In the second case, the integrity result is accepted without requiring the good result.

After the ROM integrity check passes, the module shall enter the active state.

---

## Active State

In the active state, the module shall:

- Assert the processing element fetch-enable.
- Remain in active until a reset request or a low-power entry request is received.

When a reset request or low-power entry request is received:

- the fetch-enable shall be deasserted;
- the reset cause shall be set to an undefined value;
- clock disabling shall begin.

If both a reset request and a low-power entry request are present, the reset request shall take precedence.

---

## Clock Disabling

The module shall disable main and I/O clock requests.

It must wait until every clock domain reports a status consistent with its requested disabled state.

If a direct reset request is present, the module shall proceed immediately to reset handling without waiting for the clock-disable status.

If any reset request is present after clocks are disabled, the module shall proceed to reset handling.

If no reset request is present, the module shall proceed to low-power entry handling and assert the low-power indication.

---

## Low-Power Entry Path

The low-power entry path is taken when clocks have been disabled and no reset request is present.

### Fall-Through Check

The module shall check whether the low-power entry condition is still asserted.

If the low-power entry condition has already been deasserted:

- the module shall re-enable clocks;
- assert the wakeup indication;
- assert the fall-through indication;
- return to the ROM integrity check state.

While performing this fall-through check, the module shall assert the clear-hint output.

### Non-Volatile Activity Check

If the low-power entry condition is still asserted, the module shall check whether OTP storage, the life-cycle controller, and flash storage are all idle.

If any of these are still active:

- the module shall re-enable clocks;
- assert the wakeup indication;
- assert the abort indication;
- return to the ROM integrity check state.

The low-power entry is thereby aborted.

### Low-Power Preparation

If all non-volatile blocks are idle, the module shall:

- Set the reset cause to a low-power entry cause.
- If the main power domain is off, assert reset requests for all non-always-on power domains.
- If the main power domain remains on, keep reset requests deasserted for non-always-on power domains.

The module shall wait until the reset condition is valid. The reset condition is valid when either:

- the main power domain remains on, or
- all non-always-on power domains are in reset.

### Request Power Down

Once the reset condition is valid, the module shall:

- Assert the power-down request output.
- Wait for the power-down acknowledge input.
- Deassert the power-down request.
- Enter the low-power resting state.

The low-power indication shall remain asserted throughout this path and while in the low-power state.

---

## Reset Handling Path

The reset handling path is taken when a reset request is processed.

### Enter Reset Shutdown

The module shall:

- Assert the clear-hint output.
- Set the internally tracked reset-pending condition.

### Reset Preparation

The module shall:

- Set the reset cause to a hardware reset cause.
- Assert life-cycle reset requests for all power domains for any reset request.
- Assert system reset requests for all power domains for:
  - peripheral reset requests;
  - direct reset requests;
  - software reset requests;
  - non-debug-module reset requests, except when the life-cycle design-for-test enable is active.

The module shall also:

- Assert a clear request to the companion slow-clock state machine.
- Wait for the corresponding acknowledge input.
- Wait until the reset status indicates that the reset condition is valid.

After reset preparation completes, the module shall enter the low-power resting state. Because the reset-pending condition is set, it shall immediately begin the power-up sequence without waiting for a power-up request.

During the subsequent power-up sequence:

- the power-up acknowledge shall not be asserted;
- no wakeup indication shall be generated;
- the reset-pending condition is cleared only after the power-up handshake completes.

---

## Direct Reset Requests

Direct reset requests include escalation reset requests and resets caused by main power instability.

Direct reset requests shall:

- Be treated as reset requests in the active state;
- Cause reset handling to begin without waiting for the clock-disable status to complete;
- Assert both life-cycle and system reset requests for all power domains during reset preparation.

---

## Invalid-State Behavior

If the module receives an invalid indication from the companion slow-clock state machine, or if the module itself enters an undefined state, it shall transition to a terminal state.

In the terminal state, the module shall:

- Assert reset requests for all power domains;
- Disable all clock requests;
- Hold these conditions until the system is reset.

---

## Observable Output Summary

In summary, the module must:

- Sequence clock enables and resets correctly through power-up, active, low-power, and reset paths.
- Generate a power-up acknowledge only when the companion state machine requested the power-up.
- Generate a power-down request only during low-power entry.
- Generate a wakeup indication for low-power wakeup, fall-through, and aborted low-power entry.
- Generate fall-through and abort indications only for their respective low-power exit conditions.
- Provide clear-hint and clear-configuration-lock outputs at the appropriate points in the sequences.
- Assert a strap-sample output only when strap sampling is required.
- Keep the low-power indication asserted during low-power states and cleared during normal active operation.
- Keep processing element fetch disabled except in the active state.
- Report the reset cause to the reset manager and assert the appropriate reset requests for each path.
- Forward the received hardware reset requests for reset cause recording.
